name: browser_history
description: Query a browser history database from a copy of it and its -wal, -shm and -journal sidecars, made under the job's $OUT or the agent's own directory and removed afterwards. Named queries: chrome_visits and firefox_visits (every visit joined to its URL: visit id, raw time and microsecond ISO time, transition or visit type with its raw value, referring visit), chrome_url_summary and firefox_url_summary (ONE ROW PER URL with a visit count and the last visit: a summary, not a visit list; chrome_history and firefox_history are their old names, answered with a note), chrome_downloads, firefox_downloads, tables; or your own SELECT, WITH or PRAGMA. Read-only twice: a statement must start with SELECT, WITH or PRAGMA, and the copy is opened with a SQLite authorizer that denies every action but reading and the pragmas that only report. It reports wal_present (a -wal was beside the database) and wal_frames_replayed (valid frames SQLite found in the copy of the log and checkpointed into the copy; 0 for a damaged or refused log), never merely that a sidecar was copied. Nothing in a WAL or a rollback journal names the database it was written for, so wal_inspection reads the log's own header, salts, checksums and committed frames and compares what the formats allow with the database (page size; text encoding and schema cookie from the last committed page 1); a log or journal that contradicts the database is not copied (wal_refused, journal_refused), the wal-index (-shm) is never copied, and wal_not_established says what cannot be told. The evidence may be read-only: the copies are made owner-only and writable. SENSITIVE: before any query, every trigger of the copy is dropped, then every cell of a credential column (logins.password_value, cookies.value and encrypted_value, moz_cookies.value, Firefox key4.db metadata and nssPrivate; any column whose name says password, secret, token, encrypted, card, cc, cvc, cvv, pin, ssn or iban, a number or real included; the text columns of a table named for cards or IBANs) and every text cell that is wholly a card number (13 to 19 digits passing the Luhn check) is replaced in the copy by a marker holding only its length, and the answer lists what was withheld and how many triggers were dropped. The secrets of every URL in a returned cell (a token or password in the query string, the fragment or the user-info) are replaced the same way and listed in url_secrets_withheld; write_url_secrets: true writes their whole text to a 0600 file under $OUT, in a job only. No flag brings a column value back, and nothing is decrypted. Usernames, URLs (secrets withheld) and dates are returned. A BLOB column is returned whole as hex; select what you need. A file that is not a SQLite database is answered with sqlite_header: false and its size, never its bytes.

path.description: Path to History, places.sqlite or another SQLite database

query.description: chrome_visits | chrome_url_summary | chrome_downloads | firefox_visits | firefox_url_summary | firefox_downloads | tables (chrome_history and firefox_history still answer, as the URL summaries)

sql.description: Your own SELECT, WITH or PRAGMA, instead of a named query

limit.description: Rows shown inline per statement (default 200, at most 20000, an inline page size); every row is kept, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

write_url_secrets.description: Write the whole text of every URL whose secrets were withheld, with the secret value, to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
